newsitem.title: FRANCE: DHL denies move from Brussels.
newsitem.headline: DHL denies move from Brussels.

text.p: DHL Worldwide Express said reports in the Belgian press of it considering a move from its European hub at Brussels airport were "totally unfounded."

DHL s Brussels-based spokesman on corporate affairs, Guy Collete, told Reuters the reports followed a France Presse despatch dated June 10 on the possibility of the express operator opening a Rhone/Rhine Valley sub-hub at a former military airfield at Colmar-Meyenheim.

"It's true that Colmar is one of a number of sites we are considering as the location for a sub-hub in the region but in no way does this call into question the future of our main, European hub at Brussels," Collette said.

"We are handling 800 to 900 tonnes of parcels and documents nightly at Brussels and its role as the pivotal point for a network of seven existing sub-hubs at Copenhagen, East Midlands, Nuremberg, Bergamo, Vittoria, Madrid and Cologne, is well-established."
He also dismissed reports, again from the Belgian press, that DHL was under pressure to move from Brussels airpoRt because of aircraft noise regulations in force.

"This is a non-issue. All of our planes serving Brussels are equipped with Chapter 3 hush kits and are in conformity with the relevant legislation covering aircraft noise," he stated. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
